title: Compatible idempotents on small cellular subtrees
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal, where regular means that a union of fewer than $\tau$ sets each of cardinality less than $\tau$ has cardinality less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], generated under small $\tau$-filtered colimits by a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects. Fix an object $X$. The undercategory $X/\mathcal A$ has objects $X\to V$ and commuting triangles as morphisms; its empty colimit is $1_X$. Let $T$ be a small well-founded poset, so each nonempty subset has a minimal element, and let $(X\to Y_t)_{t\in T}$ be a diagram in $X/\mathcal A$. A subset $E\subseteq T$ is downward-closed when $t\in E$ and $s\le t$ imply $s\in E$. For every downward-closed $E\subseteq T$ let $Y_E$ be its colimit in $X/\mathcal A$ and let $i_{E,F}:Y_E\to Y_F$ be the canonical map for $E\subseteq F$. Suppose every strict predecessor set $T_{<t}$ has size less than $\tau$. Suppose that for each $t$ there are $\tau$-presentable objects $P_t,Q_t$ and a pushout square in $\mathcal A$ with top arrow $P_t\to Q_t$, left arrow $P_t\to Y_{T_{<t}}$, and bottom arrow the canonical map $Y_{T_{<t}}\to Y_t$. Let $B\subseteq T$ be downward-closed, and let $e_B:Y_B\to Y_B$ and $e_T:Y_T\to Y_T$ be idempotents in $X/\mathcal A$, meaning $e_B^2=e_B$, $e_T^2=e_T$, which satisfy $i_{B,T}e_B=e_Ti_{B,T}$. For every $E_0\subseteq T$ of size less than $\tau$ there is a downward-closed $D\subseteq T$ containing $E_0$, with $|D|<\tau$, and idempotents $e_D$ on $Y_D$ and $e_{B\cap D}$ on $Y_{B\cap D}$ in $X/\mathcal A$ such that
$$
i_{D,T}e_D=e_Ti_{D,T},\qquad i_{B\cap D,B}e_{B\cap D}=e_Bi_{B\cap D,B},\qquad i_{B\cap D,D}e_{B\cap D}=e_Di_{B\cap D,D}.
$$
No presentability of $X$ or $Y_B$ is assumed.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.1.5.9, printed pp. 803-805 (using the cellular definitions of A.1.5.1-2); read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Work in the ordinary category $\mathcal K=X/\mathcal A$ throughout; compositions below are written right to left. All its Hom sets are small. It has every small colimit: adjoin a new initial indexing vertex with value $X$ and the structural arrows to the given underlying diagram, and take its colimit in $\mathcal A$. Cocones on this augmented diagram are precisely cocones under $X$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a nonempty filtered diagram the underlying colimit itself suffices: the maps from $X$ into its apex agree because any two indices have a common successor. Thus the forgetful functor $U:\mathcal K\to\mathcal A$ creates small $\tau$-filtered colimits. If downward-closed subsets increase with union $E$, their $Y$-objects have colimit $Y_E$ in $\mathcal K$: each vertex and each order arrow of $E$ occurs in one member, and compatible cocones agree at larger members. This also covers the empty tree, using $Y_\varnothing=1_X$.

source.place: A.1.5.2-3 and the union-colimit calculations used in A.1.5.8-9; explicit universal-property argument.

proof.text: For a $\tau$-presentable object $P$ of $\mathcal A$, put $F(P)=(X\to X\amalg P)$. A map under $X$ from $F(P)$ to $Z$ is exactly a map $P\to UZ$. Step 1 and presentability of $P$ show that $F(P)$ is $\tau$-presentable in $\mathcal K$. Its initial object $1_X$ is also $\tau$-presentable: its Hom functor is the singleton set, whose colimit over a nonempty filtered category is singleton (all representatives agree at a common successor). By well-founded induction, each $Y_t$ is $\tau$-presentable in $\mathcal K$. Indeed its strict predecessor diagram has fewer than $\tau$ morphisms: for an infinite set of objects use $\theta\cdot\theta=\theta$ from [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power], and the finite case is immediate. Its values are presentable by induction, so [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] makes $Y_{T_{<t}}$ presentable, including the empty case. The specified cell square is the pushout in $\mathcal K$ of $Y_{T_{<t}}\leftarrow F(P_t)\to F(Q_t)$: maps from this pushout correspond exactly to maps from the original square in $\mathcal A$ that fix $X$. The same small-colimit lemma makes $Y_t$ presentable. Finally, for any downward-closed $E$ of size less than $\tau$, apply that lemma to the restricted diagram to obtain $\tau$-presentability of $Y_E$ in $\mathcal K$. No claim of presentability of its underlying object is made.

source.place: A.1.5.8 proof, sentence asserting compactness in the undercategory; expanded using the small-colimit presentability theorem, printed pp. 802-803.

proof.text: Let $\mathscr P$ be the poset of downward-closed subsets $E\subseteq T$ of size less than $\tau$. It is small, being a subcollection of the power set of $T$. For any $S\subseteq T$ of size less than $\tau$, its downward closure is $\bigcup_{t\in S}(T_{<t}\cup\{t\})$ and has size less than $\tau$ by regularity. Also a union of fewer than $\tau$ members of $\mathscr P$ is a member, so $\mathscr P$ is $\tau$-filtered, including the empty upper-bound requirement. The diagrams $E\mapsto Y_E$ and $E\mapsto Y_{B\cap E}$ in $\mathcal K$ have colimits $Y_T$ and $Y_B$, respectively. To check this, a compatible family of cocones gives a leg for each vertex by taking its downward closure; legs are independent of this choice by unions. Every order arrow lies in one such subset, so its cocone relation holds. Conversely, restricting a cocone gives that family. The same argument applies inside $B$, since it is downward-closed. Every tail $E\supseteq E_*$ of $\mathscr P$ has these same colimits: extend a cocone on the tail by using $E\cup E_*$ for each missing $E$; unions prove independence and uniqueness.

source.place: A.1.5.8-9, the posets of small downward-closed subsets and their tails; explicit smallness, filteredness and cocone verification.

proof.text: If $Z$ is $\tau$-presentable in $\mathcal K$, its Hom functor sends either of the two tail presentations in Step 3 to a colimit of sets. Apply clauses (1)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]. Every map $Z\to Y_T$ factors through some $Y_E$ in the chosen tail, and every map $Z\to Y_B$ factors through some $Y_{B\cap E}$. Two maps from $Z$ into stages of one of these presentations which agree in its total colimit become equal after transition to a larger member of $\mathscr P$. Finitely many such factorizations and equality witnesses can all be imposed at one larger member, by taking the union of their indices. These statements concern maps in $\mathcal K$, so both factorizations and witnesses fix $X$. They apply to every small-subtree object from Step 2, without an assumption on $X$ or $Y_B$.

source.place: A.1.5.8 and A.1.5.9 compactness arguments; factorization and equality detection are expanded using Hom preservation and filtered-set clauses (1)-(3).

proof.text:
Choose $C_0$ as the downward closure of the prescribed $E_0$ and set $H_n=B\cap C_n$ whenever $C_n$ is chosen. We recursively construct increasing $C_n\in\mathscr P$ and maps $a_n:Y_{C_n}\to Y_{C_{n+1}}$, $b_n:Y_{H_n}\to Y_{H_{n+1}}$ in $\mathcal K$. Write $c_n=i_{C_n,C_{n+1}}$, $h_n=i_{H_n,H_{n+1}}$, and $j_n=i_{H_n,C_n}$. Require $i_{C_{n+1},T}a_n=e_Ti_{C_n,T}$, $i_{H_{n+1},B}b_n=e_Bi_{H_n,B}$, and $a_nj_n=j_{n+1}b_n$ for every $n$. For $n\ge1$ additionally require
$$a_nc_{n-1}=c_na_{n-1},\quad a_na_{n-1}=c_na_{n-1},\quad b_nh_{n-1}=h_nb_{n-1},\quad b_nb_{n-1}=h_nb_{n-1}.$$
These are delayed compatibility and idempotence equations; the individual maps $a_n,b_n$ are between different stages and are not asserted to be idempotents.

source.place: A.1.5.8-9, countable enlargement invariant; equivalent direct construction with partial maps instead of idempotents at intermediate stages.

proof.text: Here is the recursion step, including existence of all its equations. Once $C_n$ is given, Step 2 makes $Y_{C_n}$ and $Y_{H_n}$ presentable in $\mathcal K$. Use Step 4 on the tail above $C_n$ to factor $e_Ti_{C_n,T}$ and $e_Bi_{H_n,B}$ through $Y_F$ and $Y_{B\cap F}$ for a common $F\supseteq C_n$. Call these preliminary maps $a,b$. The maps $aj_n$ and $i_{B\cap F,F}b$ from $Y_{H_n}$ agree in $Y_T$, since $e_Ti_{B,T}=i_{B,T}e_B$. Enlarge $F$ using Step 4 to make them equal. If $n\ge1$, the maps $ac_{n-1}$ and $i_{C_n,F}a_{n-1}$ agree in $Y_T$ by the already chosen global factorization for $a_{n-1}$. The maps $aa_{n-1}$ and $i_{C_n,F}a_{n-1}$ agree there because their composites are $e_T^2i_{C_{n-1},T}$ and $e_Ti_{C_{n-1},T}$. Their source $Y_{C_{n-1}}$ is presentable, so Step 4 makes both equalities literal after enlargement. Likewise $bh_{n-1}$ and $i_{H_n,B\cap F}b_{n-1}$, and $bb_{n-1}$ and that same map, agree in $Y_B$ by the global factorization and $e_B^2=e_B$; use the $Y_B$-presentation to impose these two equalities, with presentable source $Y_{H_{n-1}}$. Take a common larger $F$, postcompose $a,b$ with the transition maps, and set $C_{n+1}=F$, $a_n=a$, $b_n=b$. Enlargements preserve every equation already imposed, since the inclusion squares commute. At $n=0$ only the first compatibility equality is imposed. Thus all stages exist, using equality witnesses rather than cancellation of nonmonic canonical maps.

source.place: A.1.5.9 proof, conditions (iii)-(v), printed pp. 804-805; explicit expansion of the omitted compactness argument, using the two-stage equations of A.1.5.8.

proof.text:
Put $D=\bigcup_{n<\omega}C_n$ and $H=\bigcup_{n<\omega}H_n=B\cap D$. Both are downward-closed, contain the required initial elements where appropriate, and have size less than $\tau$ by uncountable regularity. Step 1 identifies their objects with the colimits of the two chains. Let $u_n:Y_{C_n}\to Y_D$ and $v_n:Y_{H_n}\to Y_H$ be the canonical legs. The equations $a_{n+1}c_n=c_{n+1}a_n$ show that $u_{n+1}a_n$ are a cocone; hence they define $e_D:Y_D\to Y_D$ with $e_Du_n=u_{n+1}a_n$. Similarly obtain $e_Hv_n=v_{n+1}b_n$. Compute
$$e_D^2u_n=u_{n+2}a_{n+1}a_n=u_{n+2}c_{n+1}a_n=u_{n+1}a_n=e_Du_n.$$
The colimit uniqueness clause yields $e_D^2=e_D$. The identical calculation with $b,h,v$ gives $e_H^2=e_H$. All these are morphisms in $\mathcal K$.

source.place: A.1.5.8-9, passage to the countable union and verification of idempotence, printed pp. 803-805; explicit calculation on colimit legs.

proof.text:
Precomposing with $u_n$ and using its defining equation gives
$$i_{D,T}e_Du_n=i_{C_{n+1},T}a_n=e_Ti_{C_n,T}=e_Ti_{D,T}u_n.$$
Uniqueness for $Y_D$ proves the first required equation. The analogous computation with $v_n,b_n$ gives $i_{H,B}e_H=e_Bi_{H,B}$. Finally put $j=i_{H,D}$ and use $jv_n=u_nj_n$. Then
$$e_Djv_n=u_{n+1}a_nj_n=u_{n+1}j_{n+1}b_n=jv_{n+1}b_n=je_Hv_n.$$
Uniqueness for $Y_H$ gives $je_H=e_Dj$. Since $E_0\subseteq C_0\subseteq D$, $|D|<\tau$, and $H=B\cap D$, these are exactly the three requested compatibility equations. The empty-tree case has every object equal to $1_X$ and both induced maps its identity; the construction still applies.

source.place: A.1.5.9 conclusion, printed p. 805; all three equations checked on canonical cocone legs.
